The student at the University of Hong Kong had to "choose his courses before the deadline," but the phrase is a pun: he was pre-ordering the dishes (courses) for a formal multi-course dinner at the university, and he did pre-select them. In that evening's dinner, the courses associated with him were not served to him. The food was physically removed—plates cleared away—and other diners or staff were involved, not the student acting alone. So from his perspective, all of "his courses" were gone in one evening: the courses he had chosen for the banquet were cleared away before he could eat them. The apparent academic course-registration crisis is really a dinner-course mix-up.
